Check the project for errors without producing a binary.

Parses and type-checks the LOGOS source without invoking the full build pipeline. Useful for quick validation during development.

# Example

```bash largo check ```

Usage: largo check [OPTIONS] [FILE]

Arguments:
  [FILE]
          A LOGOS kernel-vernacular document to check (with `--kernel`) instead of the project

Options:
      --kernel
          Check FILE as a LOGOS kernel-vernacular literate document through the kernel's own document door (`Repl::execute_document`): every block, in order, stopping at the first that does not check

      --deep
          Also run rustc's analysis over the generated code (the same deep pass the IDE's flycheck uses) and translate its findings to LOGOS

      --json
          Print one `logos-check/1` JSON envelope on stdout (diagnostics with stable codes, spans, and Socratic explanations). Prose stays on stderr; exit codes are unchanged

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo check
  largo check --quiet
  largo check --kernel Demo.andSwap.lg
